title: SSHole: OpenSSH sshd password bypass on musl Linux without PAM (CVE-2026-123158)
summary: sshd in OpenSSH before 10.6p2, on Linux with musl libc and without PAM, accepts any password of 257 to 1024 bytes for an account whose password field is * (no password set, as for key-only accounts) when another local account has a $5$ or $6$ password hash. Alpine Linux is such a system. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 9 Nov 2026, with a due date of 12 Nov. Root is reachable this way only with PermitRootLogin yes, since the default is prohibit-password; another account that can become root (doas) can still reach it. Wardlatch reads files only: it never runs sshd and never connects to it.

sshd.scope: the flaw is in sshd on Linux with musl libc and without PAM (CVE-2026-123158)
sshd.fixedSource: https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/ (each branch's main.json, openssh secfixes), matching the table in Alpine's advisory

fix: Update openssh and restart sshd: apk upgrade -U -a, then rc-service sshd restart. Alpine says upgrading the package alone does not replace the running daemon. If you can't update yet, turn password logins off: set PasswordAuthentication no in your sshd configuration, check it with sshd -t, and restart sshd (Alpine's advisory gives the exact commands). To look for a break-in, Alpine says to look in /var/log/messages for sshd lines reading "Accepted password for" an account that has no password, and to review doas use and recently created users, files and authorized keys.
notCovered: Only this machine is read. sshd inside a container or an image isn't checked: a container that runs sshd on Alpine needs the same update inside it (Alpine: containers that don't run sshd are not affected). Wardlatch doesn't read logs, so it can't say whether anyone got in.
